summary: No confirmed production-code defect found in this pass. Control flow preserves allocation-success checks, uninterruptibility, upstream shouldEmit gating, the NeverInline writer, and foldable JFR-off checks. The new test is insufficient by itself to prove the native collector path or weighted accounting. Fresh exact-base/head native G1 execution remains required.

findings.title: The test can pass without exercising the changed native collector path
findings.detail: checkForJFR explicitly accepts HotSpot, accepts Serial Native Image when JFR exists, and skips Native Image when JFR is absent. No custom G1/JFR image arguments or G1 runtime assertion are attached to this test. Fresh runs of the unchanged source on HotSpot G1 and HotSpot Serial both report OK (1 test); neither can execute NativeGCAllocationSupport. Thus a generic green test result or native run with skipped JFR is not evidence for this patch.
findings.recommendation: Require a dedicated Native Image G1 image with monitoring=jfr and assert/report that the test executed under G1 with no assumption skip; demonstrate baseline failure and candidate success on identical native components. Generic Serial coverage can remain separately.

findings.title: Positive weights with throttle off do not validate native accounting or gating
findings.detail: The only weight assertion is >0 and throttle is disabled for the entire recording. Arbitrarily wrong positive weights would pass. The added test does not cover disabled event, excluded thread, active throttle, restart/reset, failed instance/array allocation, or virtual-thread carrier accounting. These matter because the new caller extends the existing writer to the native collector counter implementation.
findings.recommendation: Add controlled native G1 accounting checks with known large allocations and aggregate weight tolerances, negative/configuration cases, and failed-allocation type exclusion; test JFR-omitted and enabled-but-idle images separately for semantic/performance regressions.

production_review.successful_allocations: All four added hooks follow checkForOOME; negative array-length validation precedes the allocator. Allocation denial precedes the allocator. No new sample hook runs on null/failed allocation.
production_review.heap_safety: Callers and helper are Uninterruptible; reused writer is Uninterruptible and NeverInline. Newly allocated result stays live across the call. The call chain uses StackValue and native buffers, not a newly introduced Java allocation. G1 getThreadAllocatedMemory is a NO_TRANSITION C call. No newly introduced safepoint or Java allocation found by inspection; image analysis was not run.
production_review.configuration: shouldEmit checks recording, event enabled, throttle, and thread exclusion. Using it in the caller matches upstream guard placement and avoids timestamps/counter sampling when disabled. Uninterruptible extent protects against safepoint start/stop/reset operations. Any upstream non-safepoint configuration races or excluded-thread throttle-budget consumption are inherited, not introduced by this diff.
production_review.weights: Existing writer uses native per-thread total minus last sampled total and updates only when emitting. Native G1 implementation is delegated to svm_g1gc_get_thread_allocated_memory and not present in this public tree. Exact C implementation/ABI and monotonic inclusive accounting remain unverified.
production_review.stack_identity: NeverInline event writer retained. New helper introduces the same logical wrapper depth as existing emit; five skipped frames lead to allocation slow path. No static evidence of lost allocating method; only exact native execution can prove serialized stacks after compilation.
production_review.jfr_off: HasJfrSupport.get is @Fold and emitSample is @AlwaysInline, so a no-JFR image should eliminate the helper body. With JFR compiled in but recording disabled, one shouldEmit check remains. No native assembly or comparative throughput result was obtained.
production_review.documentation: Changed event availability footnote is consistent with intended scope; its G1 claim requires native validation before publication.
